H.Aire délimitée15 698 ha au total, dont 6:
Delimited area
15,698 ha in total, of which 6,638 ha shared with Pessac-Léognan and Cérons. The map details the 9,060 ha where Graves is the most specific appellation; Sauternes and Barsac form an enclave outside the Graves.
H.Aire délimitée17 515 ha au total, dont 8:
Delimited area
17,515 ha in total, of which 8,766 ha in the six communal appellations (Saint-Estèphe, Pauillac, Saint-Julien, Listrac-Médoc, Moulis, Margaux), whose wines may also be declared as Haut-Médoc. The map details the 8,749 ha where Haut-Médoc is the most specific appellation; the communal ones appear shaded.
H.Aire délimitée28 006 ha au total, dont 1:
Delimited area
28,006 ha in total, of which 17,697 ha in the area of the Haut-Médoc and the six communal appellations, whose wines may also be declared as Médoc. The map details the 10,309 ha where Médoc is the most specific appellation: the north of the peninsula, formerly called Bas-Médoc.
H.Aire délimitéeExactement la même aire qu:
Delimited area
Exactly the same area as Cadillac Côtes de Bordeaux (reds): 39 communes along nearly 60 km of the right bank of the Garonne, from Bassens in the north to Saint-Maixant in the south. The sweet wines Cadillac, Loupiac and Sainte-Croix-du-Mont, dotted, are separate AOCs on part of this area.
H.Aire géographique12 communes : Arbois, A:
Geographical area
12 communes: Arbois, Abergement-le-Grand, Les Arsures, Mathenay, Mesnay, Molamboz, Montigny-lès-Arsures, Les Planches-près-Arbois, Pupillin, Saint-Cyr-Montmalin, Vadans, Villette-lès-Arbois.
H.Aire géographique17 communes : 15 dans l:
Geographical area
17 communes: 15 in the Hérault (Valflaunès, Saint-Mathieu-de-Tréviers, Lauret, Claret, Les Matelles…) and Brouzet-lès-Quissac and Corconne in the Gard.
H.Aire géographique17 communes des vallées:
Geographical area
17 communes of the Tarn and Dourbie valleys around Millau, from Aguessac and Rivière-sur-Tarn to Saint-Rome-de-Tarn and Broquiès.
H.Aire géographique19 communes des Aspres,:
Geographical area
19 communes of the Aspres, between the Têt and the Tech (Thuir, Castelnou, Terrats, Trouillas, Passa…).
H.Aire géographique22 communes de part et:
Geographical area
22 communes on either side of the Garonne downstream of Agen: 12 in Lot-et-Garonne (Layrac, Astaffort, Laplume…), 7 in Tarn-et-Garonne (Auvillar, Donzac, Dunes…) and 3 in the Gers.
H.Aire géographique22 communes sur une tre:
Geographical area
22 communes along some thirty kilometres of the right bank of the Garonne, around the bastide of Cadillac. It is the southern part of the area of the Premières Côtes de Bordeaux, without the enclaves of Loupiac and Sainte-Croix-du-Mont.
H.Aire géographique23 communes : 20 en Tar:
Geographical area
23 communes: 20 in Tarn-et-Garonne (Saint-Sardos, Verdun-sur-Garonne, Beaumont-de-Lomagne, Mas-Grenier…) and 3 in Haute-Garonne (Bellesserre, Le Burgaud, Lagraulet-Saint-Nicolas).
H.Aire géographique24 communes : le secteu:
Geographical area
24 communes: the southern sector, between Meyssac, Collonges-la-Rouge, Turenne and Beaulieu-sur-Dordogne (21 communes, the only ones allowed for vin de paille), and the Vézère sector north of Brive (Allassac, Donzenac, Voutezac), the only one to carry the Coteaux de la Vézère dénomination.
H.Aire géographique28 communes de Balagne,:
Geographical area
28 communes of the Balagne, around Calvi and L’Île-Rousse, from Galéria in the south-west to Belgodère.
H.Aire géographique28 communes du centre d:
Geographical area
28 communes in the centre of the Var around Brignoles, from Saint-Maximin-la-Sainte-Baume to Barjols and the Sainte-Baume.
H.Aire géographique32 communes de l’Héraul:
Geographical area
32 communes of the Hérault, from the Cirque de Mourèze to the Buèges valley, around Aniane, Gignac, Montpeyroux, Saint-Saturnin and Saint-Jean-de-Fos.
H.Aire géographique35 communes du sud des:
Geographical area
35 communes in the south of the Landes around Geaune and Aire-sur-l’Adour, several of them in part, and Ségos in the Gers.
H.Aire géographique36 communes de Corse-du:
Geographical area
36 communes of Corse-du-Sud, from the gulf of Porto (Piana, Cargèse) to the Gravona and Prunelli valleys and the gulf of Valinco (Serra-di-Ferro).
H.Aire géographique36 communes du Vaucluse:
Geographical area
36 communes of the Vaucluse around the Luberon massif, between the Calavon valley (Apt) to the north and the Durance to the south, from Cavaillon to Manosque.
H.Aire géographique36 communes du Vic-Bilh:
Geographical area
36 communes of the Vic-Bilh: 27 in the Pyrénées-Atlantiques, 6 in the Hautes-Pyrénées (including Madiran) and 3 in the Gers, including Riscle for its delegated commune of Cannet only.
H.Aire géographique37 communes sur les cau:
Geographical area
37 communes on the causses and serres of Bas-Quercy, south of Cahors: 17 in the Lot (Montcuq, Castelnau-Montratier…) and 20 in Tarn-et-Garonne (Caussade, Montpezat-de-Quercy, Puylaroque…).
H.Aire géographique39 communes de l’Aude a:
Geographical area
39 communes of the Aude south-west of Carcassonne, around the Malepère massif and the Razès: Arzens, Montréal, Fanjeaux, Routier, Alaigne…
H.Aire géographique44 communes en arc auto:
Geographical area
44 communes in an arc around Montpellier, from Gignac and Saint-Pargoire in the west to Lunel in the east.
H.Aire géographique46 communes de l’ouest:
Geographical area
46 communes in the west of the Gers, around Plaisance, Aignan, Riscle and Saint-Mont, north of the Madiran vineyard. Some are included only in part.
H.Aire géographique49 communes, des Alpill:
Geographical area
49 communes, from the Alpilles to the Durance and the Étang de Berre, plus Artigues and Rians in the Var.
H.Aire géographique53 communes du Vaucluse:

Haut-Montravel: sweet, over 85 g/l, sémillon ≥ 50 %, 25 hl/ha (cap 30)

A soft, light rosé, often grolleau-based, suppler and less sweet than Cabernet d’Anjou.
H.Le vinRouge d'exception sur les terrasse:
The wine
An exceptional red from the dizzying terraces on the right bank at Ampuis (schistous Côte Brune, granitic Côte Blonde): deep, floral, smoky Syrah, sometimes softened with a touch of Viognier.
H.Le vinRouge de mondeuse pure, coloré, ép:
The wine
A pure Mondeuse red, deeply coloured, spicy (pepper, violet) and tannic, on the slopes of Arbin.
H.Le vinRouge de mondeuse pure, épicé et c:
The wine
A pure Mondeuse red, spicy and sturdy, on the slopes of Saint-Jean-de-la-Porte.
H.Le vinRouge exclusif de cabernet franc s:
The wine
An all-Cabernet Franc red from the left bank of the Loire, around Cléry-Saint-André.
H.Le vinRouge noir, dense et solaire de pu:
The wine
An inky, dense, sun-drenched red of pure Syrah, from the curved granite slopes of the single commune of Cornas — “burnt earth” in Celtic, one of the great age-worthy wines of the Rhône.
H.Le vinRouges charpentés de grenache au p:
The wine
Sturdy Grenache reds at the foot of the Dentelles de Montmirail — spice, garrigue and black fruit; generous rosés and, since 2023, a few Clairette whites.
H.Le vinRouges de gamay souples et blancs:
The wine
Supple Gamay reds and Jacquère whites, on the Chautagne slopes north of the Lac du Bourget.
H.Le vinRouges de garde, à la robe soutenu:
The wine
Reds for ageing, deep in colour, structured, with aromas of very ripe red fruit and black fruit (cahier des charges).
H.Le vinRouges secs, riches et solaires de:
The wine
Rich, sun-drenched dry Grenache reds on the clay-limestone slopes of Rasteau, promoted to cru in 2010 — on the same land as the historic vin doux naturel.
H.Le vinRouges seuls, sur les terres rouge:
The wine
Reds only, on the red soils (Triassic) and sandstone south of the Dentelles: deep Grenache and Syrah. Distinct from the famous Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise (white VDN).
H.Le vinRéservée aux rouges, sur la moitié:
The wine
Reserved for reds, in the northern half (Agly valley); concentrated blends. Five village dénominations: Caramany, Latour-de-France, Lesquerde, Tautavel and Les Aspres.
H.Le vinSauvignon de la rive droite de la:
The wine
Sauvignon from the right bank of the Loire, facing Sancerre, on flint (“pierre à fusil”) and Kimmeridgian marl; a racy white with smoky notes.
H.Le vinSur le massif de la Malepère, à l':
The wine
On the Malepère massif, west of Carcassonne: Atlantic influence, reds based on Merlot and Cabernet Franc.
H.Le vinSur les arènes granitiques du golf:
The wine
On the decomposed granite of the Gulf of Ajaccio and the Gravona valley: fine, peppery reds led by the local Sciaccarellu, delicate rosés and Vermentinu whites.
H.Le vinSur les contreforts des monts du F:
The wine
On the foothills of the Monts du Forez, south of Montbrison: Gamay only, as fruity reds and lively rosés.
H.Le vinSur les coteaux argilo-calcaires d:
The wine
On the clay-limestone slopes of the Nebbio, at the foot of Cap Corse (Gulf of Saint-Florent): great Niellucciu reds (a cousin of Sangiovese), rosés and 100% Vermentinu whites — the birthplace of Corsican AOCs (1968).
H.Le vinSur les coteaux argilo-calcaires à:
The wine
On clay-limestone slopes straddling the Gers, Hautes-Pyrénées and Béarn: a powerful, tannic Tannat red, dark and sturdy, that softens with age.
H.Le vinSur les coteaux du Cher et de l'Ar:
The wine
On the slopes of the Cher and the Arnon: Sauvignon for whites, Pinot Noir for reds, and a renowned Pinot Gris rosé.
H.Le vinSur les deux rives du Tarn autour:
The wine
On both banks of the Tarn around Albi: a unique palette — dry, sweet and perlé whites of Mauzac and Loin de l'Œil, Duras and Braucol reds, ancestral-method sparkling wines.
H.Le vinSur les fortes pentes de la boucle:
The wine
On the steep slopes of the bend of the Rhône (Briord, Montagnieu, Seillonnaz): lively white sparkling and semi-sparkling wines and Mondeuse reds.
H.Le vinSur les pentes granitiques dominan:
The wine
On the granite slopes above Roanne and the Loire: Gamay (called “Saint-Romain”) as generous reds and rosés.
H.Le vinSur les reliefs du Luberon, au sud:
The wine
On the Luberon hills, south of the Durance: fresh whites and rosés play a big part (high-altitude climate), alongside supple Grenache and Syrah reds.
H.Le vinSur les restanques en amphithéâtre:
The wine
On the amphitheatre of terraces (restanques) around the bay of Bandol: powerful, tannic Mourvèdre reds for long ageing (18 months in large casks), renowned food-friendly rosés and rare whites.
H.Le vinSur les rougiers (grès rouges) au:
The wine
On the rougiers (red sandstone) north of Rodez: a unique Fer Servadou red, peppery, raspberry-scented and rustic — the wine of the Aveyron.
H.Le vinSur les schistes du nord de Bézier:
The wine
On the schist north of Béziers; spicy, mineral reds and increasingly sought-after whites.
H.Le vinSur les schistes en terrasses vert:
The wine
On the dizzying schist terraces of Cap Corse: lively Vermentinu whites and rare reds, alongside the Muscats of the Cap.
H.Le vinSur les terrasses de la Garonne en:
The wine
On the Garonne terraces between Toulouse and Montauban: Négrette reds and rosés with violet, liquorice and black-fruit aromas.
H.Le vinSur les terrasses granitiques du S:
The wine
On the granite terraces of the Sartenais and the Rizzanese valley: structured Sciaccarellu and Niellucciu reds, in “the most Corsican of towns”.
H.Le vinSur les terroirs frais au pied de:
The wine
On the cool terroirs at the foot of Mont Sainte-Victoire (Aix): more structured rosés and reds, shaped by altitude and wide temperature swings.
H.Le vinSélection de rouges de cabernet (f:
The wine
A selection of Cabernet reds (Franc and Sauvignon) from Anjou's best terroirs, more concentrated and age-worthy.
H.Le vinTerroir calcaire de Tautavel et Vi:
The wine
The limestone terroir of Tautavel and Vingrau; powerful, structured reds for ageing.
H.Le vinTerroir de gneiss autour de Carama:
The wine
A gneiss terroir around Caramany, in the Agly valley; supple reds, with Carignan made by carbonic maceration.
H.Le vinTerroir de sables granitiques auto:
The wine
A granitic-sand terroir around Lesquerde, west of the Agly; fine, fragrant reds.
H.Le vinTerroir des Aspres, au sud de la T:
The wine
The Aspres terroir, south of the Têt; warm reds requiring a large share of Mourvèdre and Syrah.
H.Le vinTrois communes en boucle du Lot au:
The wine
Three communes in a bend of the Lot around the village of Estaing: Fer Servadou and Gamay reds and rosés, Chenin and Mauzac whites.
H.Le vinTrois communes à l'est d'Aix-en-Pr:
The wine
Three communes east of Aix-en-Provence, on the Langesse limestone: age-worthy reds, original whites and rosés from a conservatory of old Provençal grapes — led by a handful of estates.
H.Le vinUn des plus anciens blancs du Lang:
The wine
One of the oldest whites in the Languedoc (Hérault valley): dry, medium-sweet or rancio Clairette.
H.Le vinUn petit vignoble du Bas-Limousin,:
The wine
A small vineyard of Bas-Limousin, on the edge of the Périgord: cabernet franc reds on the red sandstones around Meyssac and Turenne, dry chenin whites on the Vézère schists, and the rare vin de paille, an amber sweet wine from dried grapes.
H.Le vinUne ancienne île devenue massif, b:
The wine
A former island turned massif, beaten by wind and sea spray: saline bourboulenc whites and garrigue reds.
H.Le vinVaste appellation autour d'Aix-en-:
The wine
A large appellation around Aix-en-Provence, from the Durance to the Étang de Berre: Mediterranean-blend rosés and reds (with a touch of Cabernet), and Rolle whites — a windy, sunny vineyard.
H.Le vinVaste appellation du Saumurois sur:
The wine
A large Saumurois appellation on tuffeau: Chenin whites, Cabernet reds and above all fine bubbles (Saumur mousseux / brut).
H.Le vinVieux vignoble du Bourbonnais sur:
The wine
An old Bourbonnais vineyard on the banks of the Sioule and the Allier: Gamay and Pinot Noir reds/rosés, Tressallier (Sacy), Chardonnay and Sauvignon whites.
H.Le vinVignoble de l'Ain entre Bugey et c:
The wine
The Ain vineyard between the Bugey and the Usses gorge: Chardonnay and Altesse whites, Gamay, Mondeuse and Pinot reds, rosés and above all fine bubbles — including the famous Cerdon.
H.Le vinVignoble de piémont au sud des Lan:
The wine
A foothill vineyard in the south of the Landes (Geaune, Aire-sur-l'Adour): whites from the local Baroque grape, Tannat and Cabernet reds and rosés.
H.Le vinVignoble des deux rives de la Loir:
The wine
A vineyard on both banks of the Loire at Ancenis: Gamay reds and rosés, and above all the medium-sweet Malvoisie (Pinot Gris) white.
H.Le vinVillage-phare de la Combe de Savoi:
The wine
The leading village of the Combe de Savoie: Jacquère whites and Mondeuse/Gamay reds, on the slopes beneath its towers.
H.Le vinVin doux naturel de grenache noir:
The wine
A Grenache Noir vin doux naturel on the black schist of the Agly valley (Maury); fruity grenat or oxidative tuilé. Also made as dry Maury (red).
H.Le vinVin doux naturel de muscat (petits:
The wine
A Muscat vin doux naturel (petits grains + Alexandrie), fortified to keep the fresh-grape aroma; the largest Muscat vineyard in France.
H.Le vinVin doux naturel de muscat à petit:
The wine
A vin doux naturel from Muscat à petits grains (white and red), fortified to keep the aroma of fresh grapes and roses — one of France's great Muscats, at the foot of the Dentelles.

The wine
A vin doux naturel from Muscat à petits grains on the schist of Cap Corse and the Nebbio: fortified on the skins, golden, intensely aromatic (fresh grapes, candied citrus, flowers) — one of the island's jewels.

The wine
Muscat à petits grains vin doux naturel, between Montpellier and Nîmes. Grapes at 252 g/l at least, 110 g/l of sugars and at least 15 % actual alcohol after fortification.
H.Le vinVin doux naturel sur les terrasses:
The wine
A vin doux naturel on schist terraces overlooking the sea (Collioure, Banyuls, Port-Vendres, Cerbère); fortified Grenache, in rimage (fruity) and traditional oxidative styles.
H.Le vinVin gris historique aux portes de:
The wine
A historic vin gris at the gates of Tours: a blend of the three Pinots (Meunier, Gris, Noir), dry and delicate.
H.Le vinVoisin de Gigondas sur la plaine e:
The wine
Gigondas's neighbour on the plain and terraces: warm, spicy Grenache and Syrah reds, a few rosés and whites — the most affordable cru of the Dentelles.
H.Le vinVoisine occidentale de Sancerre su:
The wine
Sancerre's western neighbour on the same Kimmeridgian marl: straight Sauvignon for whites, Pinot Noir for reds and rosés.
H.Le vinÀ l'extrême ouest de la Dordogne,:
The wine
At the far west of the Dordogne, bordering the Bordelais: lively dry Sauvignon-Sémillon whites and, since 2001, Merlot-led reds.
H.Le vinÀ l'extrême sud, entre Sartène et:
The wine
In the far south, between Sartène and Bonifacio: one of Corsica's oldest vineyards, wind-swept, on granite — concentrated reds and rosés, saline whites.
H.Le vinÀ la limite du Berry : blancs de s:
The wine
On the edge of the Berry: Sauvignon whites, Gamay, Côt and Pinot Noir reds, on the slopes of the Cher.

H.Les Baux-de-ProvenceL’AOC Les Baux-de-Pr:
Les Baux-de-Provence
The AOC Les Baux-de-Provence lies almost entirely within the area (99 %), on the northern slope of the Alpilles: its parcels have their own colour, within a dashed boundary.
H.Les appellations de l’aireCinq aires plu:
The appellations of the area
Five smaller areas lie within that of Bergerac: Pécharmant (reds), Rosette (medium-sweet whites), Monbazillac and Saussignac (sweet wines) and Montravel, which contains the shared area of Côtes de Montravel and Haut-Montravel. Their parcels each have their own colour and their line in the list. Pécharmant parcels also located in Rosette (81 % of its area) are shown as Pécharmant.
H.Les appellations de l’aireDeux AOC plus:
The appellations of the area
Two smaller AOCs lie entirely within the area: Boutenac (reds, around Lézignan) and Fitou (reds, in the south-east). Their parcels have their own colour and their line in the list.
H.Les appellations de l’aireMinervois-La L:
The appellations of the area
Minervois-La Livinière (reds) lies entirely within the area, as does 96 % of Muscat de Saint-Jean-de-Minervois. Their parcels have their own colour and their line in the list.
H.Les dénominationsLe cahier des charges p:
The dénominations
The cahier des charges provides for five additional geographical dénominations: Cru Sainte-Victoire, Fréjus, La Londe, Pierrefeu and Notre-Dame des Anges. The INAO publishes the area only for Cru Sainte-Victoire and La Londe: their parcels have their own colour and their line in the list. Fréjus, Pierrefeu and Notre-Dame des Anges are not there yet.

Terraces
Many vines are planted on terraces on the red sandstone slopes. For them the minimum density does not apply and the yield is calculated at 3 m² per planted vine.
H.TerroirButtes de graves garonnaises déco:
Terroir
Hillocks of Garonne gravel cut into mounds (the « cos ») by the esteys and jalles, and, more than further south, Tertiary clay-limestone soils, as at the Couquèques anticline.
H.TerroirComme tout l’Entre-deux-Mers, un:
Terroir
Like all of the Entre-deux-Mers, a Tertiary limestone plateau covered with sands, gravels and clays brought by the Garonne and the Dordogne, here above the Garonne slopes, between Cadillac and Sauveterre-de-Guyenne.
H.TerroirCoteaux argilo-calcaires abrupts:
Terroir
Steep clay-limestone slopes facing the Garonne, gravels on the low terraces, rolling plateaus towards the Entre-deux-Mers.
H.TerroirCoteaux argilo-calcaires et « sab:
Terroir
Clay-limestone slopes and « Périgord sands »; the climate becomes more continental there than in the rest of the Côtes de Bordeaux.
H.TerroirCoteaux argilo-calcaires qui domi:
Terroir
Clay-limestone slopes overlooking the estuary, with outcrops of starfish limestone, then sands and gravels inland; palus (alluvial flats) along the Gironde.
H.TerroirCoteaux de calcaire à astéries en:
Terroir
Starfish-limestone slopes cut by a network of streams (Picampeau hill, 81 m). Fronsadais molasses on the slopes, sands and gravels to the north-west.
H.TerroirCoteaux et vallons bien exposés e:
Terroir
Well-exposed slopes and small valleys along the Dordogne and its tributaries. The river creates a mild, humid microclimate there, with night-time mists at the end of summer.
H.TerroirCoteaux et vallons culminant à 92:
Terroir
Slopes and small valleys rising to 92 m, drained by the Brouillon and the Moron. Red « terre de Sienne » silts on the plateaus, sandy-clay gravels on the slopes, mostly clay-limestone, and a limestone cornice facing the estuary. Sunnier and drier than the Bordeaux average.
H.TerroirCoteaux très accidentés, parallèl:
Terroir
Very rugged slopes, parallel to the river and cut by its tributaries. Starfish limestone at the bottom of the slope (it carries the town of Saint-Macaire), then Agenais molasses and, at the top, the sands and gravels bordering the Entre-deux-Mers.
H.TerroirCroupes de graves et de galets ro:
Terroir
Mounds of gravel and pebbles laid down by the ancient Garonne, sometimes three metres thick, over limestone and faluns. Many vineyards are enclaves within the urban area.
H.TerroirCroupes de graves garonnaises le:
Terroir
Mounds of Garonne gravel along the estuary, more clay-limestone inland and to the north. Five growths classified in 1855 outside the communal appellations: La Lagune, Cantemerle, La Tour Carnet, Belgrave, Camensac.
H.TerroirCroupes de graves garonnaises plu:
Terroir
Mounds of Garonne gravel more clayey than at Pauillac, on a limestone base that outcrops in places, facing the estuary.
H.TerroirCroupes de graves, d’argiles et d:
Terroir
Mounds of gravel, clay and limestone between the Garonne and the Landes forest. The cold waters of the Ciron meet the warmer Garonne: autumn mists favour botrytis.
H.TerroirDes tertres et des coteaux : mola:
Terroir
Hillocks and slopes: Fronsadais molasses at the base, a cornice of Castillon limestone, then starfish limestone on the plateau. The Fronsac hillock rises to 76 m. The alluvial plains are excluded.
H.TerroirDeux grands plateaux de graves pr:
Terroir
Two large plateaus of deep gravel, north and south of the town, separated by the Gaër channel. Three of the five 1855 first growths are here.
H.TerroirEntre les graves du nord, typique:
Terroir
Between the northern gravels, typical of the Graves, and the clay-limestone over starfish limestone of the south, as at Barsac. Its own feature: mounds of residual gravel on a clay-limestone base, separated by sandy hollows.
H.TerroirGalets, graviers et sables mêlés:
Terroir
Pebbles, gravel and sand mixed with silt and clay, over limestone, pure sand or alios (iron-rich sand). The appellation takes its name from these gravels (graves).
H.TerroirLe prolongement du plateau calcai:
Terroir
The continuation of the Saint-Émilion limestone plateau and its clay-limestone slopes, with sands and gravels descending towards the Dordogne.
H.TerroirMolasses du Fronsadais au pied de:
Terroir
Fronsadais molasses at the foot of the slopes, a wooded cornice of Castillon limestone, starfish limestone on the plateau. The low alluvial valley of the Dordogne is excluded.
H.TerroirMoyennes terrasses de l’Isle : sa:
Terroir
Middle terraces of the Isle: sand, gravel and pebbles in a sandy-clay matrix, with crasse de fer in the subsoil as at Pomerol.
H.TerroirPlateau calcaire tertiaire recouv:
Terroir
A Tertiary limestone plateau covered with sands, gravels and clays brought by the Garonne and the Dordogne. The name comes from the « two seas »: the tidal influence reaches up both rivers.
H.TerroirPlateau de calcaire à astéries où:
Terroir
A starfish-limestone plateau on which Montagne, Saint-Georges and Parsac are built, cut by the Barbanne. Fronsadais molasses on the slopes and sands and gravels to the west.
H.TerroirRelief escarpé jusqu’à 120 m. Sou:
Terroir
Steep relief up to 120 m. Below the château and the church, a limestone cliff overlooks the Garonne, with a bank of fossil oysters (Ostrea aquitanica) hollowed into caves where wine is kept. A limestone plateau sloping south-west, drained by the Padouen.
H.TerroirRelief marqué (jusqu’à 120 m) : p:
Terroir
Marked relief (up to 120 m): starfish-limestone plateaus, clay-limestone slopes, foot-slopes and a gravel plain towards the river, drained by many streams.
H.TerroirRelief marqué jusqu’à 120 m : cal:
Terroir
Marked relief up to 120 m: starfish limestone under sandy-gravelly decalcification clays, clay-limestone slopes and gravels at the foot of the slopes, drained by many streams towards the Garonne.
H.TerroirRelief marqué, jusqu’à plus de 10:
Terroir
Marked relief, up to more than 100 m: a limestone plateau overlooking the Garonne with a south-west-facing slope, cut by the small valleys of the Ricaud and the Matelot; little vine-covered hills and wooded valleys.
H.TerroirTable de calcaire à astéries jusq:
Terroir
A starfish-limestone table up to 100 m high, cut by the Barbanne. Fronsadais molasses at the foot of the slopes.
H.TerroirTerrasses de graves et de sables:
Terroir
Terraces of gravel and sand over clay, with a subsoil rich in iron oxides, the crasse de fer.
H.TerroirTerrasses de graves sur la rive g:
Terroir
Gravel terraces on the left bank of the estuary, the leanest in the Médoc. It is the appellation with the most growths classified in 1855.
H.TerroirUn plateau bas de calcaire à asté:
Terroir
A low plateau of starfish limestone under a thin layer of red clayey sand. Where the cold Ciron joins the warmer Garonne, autumn mists favour botrytis. Two first growths: Climens and Coutet.
H.TerroirUn plateau culminant à 43 m, le p:
Terroir
A plateau rising to 43 m, the highest point of the Médoc, between the Fonréaud mound to the south and the Fourcas mound to the north.
H.TerroirUn plateau de 20 à 30 m entaillé:
Terroir
A plateau of 20 to 30 m cut by the Gestas and the Souloire, on sandy clays and siliceous gravels: sandy or clay-gravel soils that give the appellation its name.
H.TerroirUn plateau de calcaire à astéries:
Terroir
A starfish-limestone plateau around the town, clay-limestone slopes on molasse, then gravels and sands towards Pomerol and the Dordogne plain.
H.TerroirUn seul bloc de croupes graveleus:
Terroir
A single block of gravel mounds between Pauillac and Margaux, almost entirely under vine. No first growth, but a high proportion of classed growths.
H.TerroirUn étroit ruban de douze kilomètr:
Terroir
A narrow ribbon twelve kilometres long perpendicular to the estuary, between Margaux and Saint-Julien: the westernmost of the communal appellations, with no frontage on the Gironde.
H.TerroirUne terrasse de galets roulés mêl:
Terroir
A terrace of rounded pebbles mixed with red sandy clay, described by the cahier des charges as the largest Villafranchian terrace in Europe.

Parcels that also carry Muscadet Sèvre et Maine, Muscadet Coteaux de la Loire or Muscadet Côtes de Grandlieu each have their own colour and line in the list. Their areas extend slightly beyond that of generic Muscadet: those parcels appear only on their own page.

Cabernet d’Anjou, Rosé d’Anjou and Anjou share exactly the same delimited area published by the INAO (36,189 ha): these parcels may produce either appellation.

Anjou, Cabernet d’Anjou and Rosé d’Anjou share exactly the same delimited area published by the INAO (36,189 ha). The more specific appellations of Anjou (Savennières, Layon, Anjou Villages…) have their own pages.

H.Villages nommésVingt villages peuvent ac:
Named villages
Twenty villages may add their name to the appellation (geographical dénomination). Each has its colour on the map, its line in the list and its own page. Chusclan is reserved for reds and rosés; Gadagne, Massif d’Uchaux, Nyons, Plan de Dieu, Puyméras, Saint-Andéol, Sainte-Cécile, Signargues, Suze-la-Rousse and Vaison-la-Romaine for reds. Visan is a special case: the INAO publishes no delimited Villages area in this commune. Its area is reconstructed here (see its page), and it is added to the Villages area.

H.⚠ Aire délimitée non publiéeL’AOC Saint-:
⚠ Delimited area not published
The AOC Saint-Sardos does have a parcel area, approved by the national committee on 8 and 9 June 2005 and filed at the town halls, but it is not in the INAO open data. This map therefore shows the vines actually planted in the 23 communes of the geographical area, according to the IGN BD TOPO and the 2024 graphical parcel register. It is an approximation of the delimited area.
H.⚠ Aire reconstituéeL’INAO ne publie pas:
⚠ Reconstructed area
The INAO publishes no delimited area for Côtes du Rhône Villages in Visan: on this commune its parcel file carries only the Côtes du Rhône area (3,427 ha). The Villages cahier des charges (2024) gives the whole commune of Visan as the geographical area of the « Visan » dénomination. Yet for the nine single-commune named villages that the INAO does publish (Séguret, Sablet, Valréas, Roaix, Rochegude, Saint-Gervais, Saint-Maurice, Saint-Pantaléon, Rousset), the village area is identical to the commune’s Côtes du Rhône area (difference of 0 to 3 ha). The Visan area is therefore reconstructed as the Côtes du Rhône area of the commune of Visan. To be confirmed with the INAO or the town hall, which holds the plans.

⚠ Reconstructed area
The INAO does not publish the parcel area of Bellet. The cahier des charges defines a perimeter of 16 lieux-dits of Nice: the map brings together the corresponding cadastral lieux-dits (Crémat, Saquier, Lingostière, Li Punccias, Candeou, Saint-Roman, Saint-Sauveur, Golfan, Canta Galet, Les Cappans…) and fills the small gaps between them. « Le Grand Bois » and « Serre-Long » have no equivalent in the land registry. The vines actually delimited are part of this perimeter.

⚠ Reconstructed area
The INAO does not publish the parcel area of Cassis. The map therefore shows the whole commune of Cassis, which is the geographical area of the cahier des charges. The delimited vines cover only a small part of it, between the town, Cap Canaille and the calanques.
H.⚠ Carte approximativeIl n’existe pas d’a:
⚠ Approximate map
There is no published delimited area for the Puy-Notre-Dame dénomination. Its wines come from identified parcels: each year, before 31 January, each producer declares the parcels assigned to the dénomination, according to criteria set by the INAO on 29 May 2008 (slopes, clay-limestone soils). The map therefore shows the Saumur area of the eleven former communes of the dénomination’s geographical area: where it may be produced, not the parcels actually identified, which are only part of it.
H.⚠ DélimitationL’INAO n’a pas publié d’ai:
⚠ Delimitation
The INAO has not published a delimited parcel area for Sainte-Foy (checked in its data of 21 and 28 September 2026). The cahier des charges refers to identified parcels, whose list can be consulted at the INAO offices. This map therefore shows the 19 communes of the geographical area with all their cadastral parcels: none is presented as being inside or outside the AOC.
H.⚠ Pas d’aire délimitéeL’AOC Corrèze n’a:
⚠ No delimited area
The AOC Corrèze has no published parcel area: each year, at the growers’ request, the INAO identifies the parcels that meet the criteria set by the national committee on 8 June 2016. This map therefore shows the vines actually planted in the 24 communes of the geographical area, according to the IGN BD TOPO and the 2024 graphical parcel register. It is an approximation: a vine on the map is not necessarily identified as AOC, and vice versa.
